sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Statutory Basis**: Governed by Section 42(1) of the **RBI Act, 1934**, requiring scheduled commercial banks to maintain an average daily balance with the RBI.
• **Nature of Deposits**: Calculated as a percentage of a bank's **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)**.
• **Interest Payment**: Banks **do not earn any interest** on the CRR balances maintained with the RBI, making it a cost for the banking system.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Serves as a direct quantitative tool for liquidity management and inflation control under the **Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF)** ecosystem.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Maintained strictly in liquid cash form as a percentage of NDTL with the RBI.

items.definition: The liability of a bank to other banks and the public, categorized into demand liabilities (payable on demand) and time liabilities (payable with advance notice).
Banks included in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934, which are legally mandated to maintain CRR with the RBI.
Statutory body under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act, 1934, responsible for fixing the benchmark interest rates, which work in tandem with CRR adjustments.
The principal legislative backing that empowers the RBI to mandate, inspect, and penalize banks for non-maintenance of CRR.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Nationwide Uniformity**: CRR is applied uniformly across all Scheduled Commercial Banks throughout the territory of India, irrespective of regional location or state boundaries.
• **Exception / Special Categories**: Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) and Local Area Banks also maintain CRR as mandated by RBI directives, though cooperative banks have distinct regulatory structures under state/central dual control.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: High CRR increases the cost of funds for banks, potentially raising lending rates for consumers and affecting credit growth.
• **Policy Interventions**: The removal of the lower limit floor (previously fixed at 3% under the repealed Narasimham Committee recommendations era, now with no statutory minimum floor post-2006 amendments) provides RBI greater operational flexibility.

items.title: Mnemonic for Reserve Ratios (CRR vs SLR)
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'C-R-R is Cash with RBI, S-L-R is Safe-assets Locally Kept'.
• **Decoded Meaning**: CRR must be kept as Cash with the Central Bank (RBI), whereas SLR can be kept in safe assets (G-secs, gold) within the bank itself.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly eliminates incorrect options swapping where assets or holding institutions are confused.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Raising CRR reduces money multiplier effect and drains liquidity; lowering CRR injects liquidity into the banking system.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that 'Banks earn interest on CRR balances maintained with the RBI.' This is completely false. Banks do NOT earn any interest on CRR.

Mains Value Addition: In GS-3 answers on inflation or monetary transmission, argue how an optimal CRR strikes a balance between systemic safety and avoiding 'financial repression' of commercial banking profitability.

keyTakeaways: CRR is a mandatory percentage of NDTL that scheduled commercial banks must keep with the RBI.
It earns zero interest for commercial banks, acting as a direct instrument for liquidity mop-up and monetary policy execution.
Changes in CRR directly alter the money multiplier and overall credit creation capacity of the economy.
